title: TESS sectors 101 and 102 (2026) do not show the reported flare excess of HIP 67522 near planet transit: 3 of 17 flares occur at orbital phase 0 to 0.2, against 64 percent predicted
abstract:
Question: Ilin et al. (2025, Nature) reported that flares on the young star HIP 67522 cluster at orbital phase 0 to 0.2 after the transit of its planet HIP 67522 b. They used TESS sectors 11, 38 and 64 and CHEOPS data, and they interpreted the result as magnetic star-planet interaction. TESS observed the star again in sectors 101 and 102 (March to April 2026, 43.7 days). We used these new data as an out-of-sample test, with all model parameters fixed from the paper.

Method: We fitted a new transit ephemeris to 17 transits. We detected flares in the 2-min PDCSAP light curves with the criterion of Ilin et al. (3 points at 3 sigma or more). We vetted the flares with target-pixel difference images and background data. We put our energies on the scale of Ilin et al. with the 12 TESS flares that they listed; our pipeline recovered all 12. We compared the in-window flare fraction with the exposure share and with the model prediction. We did injection-recovery, posterior-predictive and scan-statistic tests, and an independent detection in the 20-s data.

Result: For flares with E of 1e34 erg or more, 3 of 17 new flares are in the window. The exposure share is 22 percent, and the published model predicts 64 percent (binomial p = 1.1e-4; log10 Bayes factor -3.4 against the model). None of the 6 new flares with E of 10^34.5 erg or more is in the window (3.9 predicted; completeness 87 to 100 percent). The 20-s data show 0 of 8 flare events in the window. The new phases agree with a uniform distribution (Kuiper p = 0.84). Detection completeness does not depend on phase. In all five sectors together, 13 of 42 flares are in the window (p = 0.076 against uniform phases).

Limitations: The new sample is small. When we include the published parameter uncertainty, the rejection is near 2 sigma (posterior-predictive p = 0.04 to 0.07). Our flare selection is not identical to that of the original study. We did not re-analyse the CHEOPS data. Intermittent star-planet interaction is not excluded. display.caption: Flare rate (E of 1e34 erg or more) as a function of the orbital phase of HIP 67522 b. Left: TESS sectors 11, 38 and 64, which are the data of the claim. Right: new sectors 101 and 102 (2026). The grey band is the claimed window (phase 0 to 0.2). The solid line is the published two-rate model, and the dashed line is the published flat rate. Error bars are 68 percent Poisson intervals. Ticks show the flare phases. The new sectors have 3 of 17 flares in the window, near the exposure share of 22 percent.

Fraction of flares at phase 0 to 0.2 as a function of the minimum flare energy (Ilin et al. energy scale). Blue: sectors of the claim. Orange: new 2026 sectors. Error bars are 68 percent binomial intervals. Dashed line: exposure share (uniform phases). Solid line: prediction of the published model. Above 10^34.5 erg, where completeness is 87 percent or more, the new sectors have 0 of 6 flares in the window.

Detrended TESS 2-min light curves of HIP 67522 in sectors 101 and 102, with the transit model removed. Grey bands show the claimed window. Triangles mark detected flares; orange triangles mark flares with E of 1e34 erg or more. One candidate at BTJD 4138.35 is a background event and is not marked.
